text:
anya: Heads-up — ran into a weird perf regression on the 8k burst workload after last night's kernel-autotune tweak. p50 jumped in steady-state when continuous batching is enabled.

samir: Oh no. Which tweak? the new arch-aware scoring?

anya: Yeah, the autotuner started preferring the tile-opt kernel for mid/long sequences based on single-op throughput. That looks good in isolation, but in our continuous-batching traces we see more frequent short launches and the tile-opt path has a higher launch overhead + KV cache rebinds.

kevin: Can you paste numbers?

anya: Sure. baseline (old scoring) with cont-batch on: p50=18ms, p95=62ms for 64 concurrent streams, average seqlen 120. After autotune change: p50=29ms, p95=95ms, CPU/GPU launch stalls visible.

marta: That delta is big. Any profile traces?

perf-bot: perf snapshot uploaded: https://internal/perf/1965432100 (instrumentation: nvtx + trace event)

anya: core snippet from the trace (top shows frequent kernel-switch points and KV invalidate calls):

```
[trace] stream-23: launch(tile-opt) -> kernel_init (2.1ms) -> kv.bind() -> forward (0.8ms)
[trace] stream-23: next request arrives -> small-prefix hit -> fallback to cont-path -> launch(cont-opt) -> kernel_init (1.9ms) -> kv.rebind()
```

anya: The problem is the autotune changed the stable mapping so the scheduler alternates between tile-opt and cont-opt on similar seqlens, causing extra kernel_init and KV rebinds.

samir: So it's a churn problem, not raw kernel perf. The cost is amortized launch + KV synchronization.

kevin: We saw KV cache warmup costs before but not this often. The autotuner's hysteresis must be too weak.

marta: Two quick hypotheses: (A) scoring ignores launch amortization and per-launch init cost, (B) sequence-length buckets in the tuner are too coarse and straddle both kernels.

samir: Proposed mitigations: 1) add launch_overhead term to score (measured as kernel_init mean), 2) require a min-stability window (e.g., 30s) before switching kernels for a given worker, 3) prefer kernel pinning per-request-family to avoid mid-stream flips.

anya: I prototyped 1) locally: when we penalize tile-opt by +1.2ms launch, p50 returns to ~19ms. But p95 still slightly higher — probably residual KV thrash.

kevin: Can we avoid KV rebind on kernel switch? Maybe keep kv cache layout compatible or defer rebind until idle.

marta: Defer rebind sounds promising: if we detect an immediate flip back, skip rebind and run cont-path via software fallback for one request. That trades a tiny compute hit for avoiding repeated init.

samir: Also add detection to autotuner: if recent switching rate > threshold, temporarily widen the bucket and prefer the kernel with lower launch cost.

anya: I'll run an A/B with these changes on a canary pool. Plan: autotune scoring + hysteresis + deferred-kv-rebind. Rolling to 10% traffic, 1h runs.

kevin: Ping ops if you need to roll back. I can add a dashboard tile that shows kernel switch rate and KV rebinds per worker.

marta: One more ask: include a tiny synthetic that exercises bursty 8k seqlen traffic (repeat prefix patterns) so tuner sees realistic distribution. Otherwise it will keep oscillating.

anya: Good call. I'll attach the synthetic and results. Will post updates here. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: experiment started on canary-3 (10%): 1965432160

samir: Thanks — please keep the trace links in the experiment notes so we can compare pre/post.

anya: Will do. If this fixes it, we should land a quick patch to the autotuner and add an integration test to catch kernel-churn regressions.

kevin: Sounds good. If the deferred-rebind helps, we should consider it as a permanent guard in the runtime.

marta: Agreed. Low-risk, high payoff.

anya: Update (1965432375): initial A/B completed. p50 back to 19ms, p95 improved to 70ms. Kernel switch events down ~78%. Uploading full traces in 5.

samir: Nice! commit PR?

anya: Opening PR now with scoring penalty + 30s hysteresis + deferred-rebind flag (off by default until we validate). PR link: https://git.redwood/pr/4521

marta: Reviewing. Thanks everyone.
